bull.b: Revenue growth is supported by larger enterprise relationships, not only broader SMB demand: $50k+ ARR customers grew 36% and now contribute about 40% of ARR. This mix can deepen retention, expand wallet share, and make growth more durable as Klaviyo moves upmarket.

Operating cash flow of about $310M and free cash flow of about $285M, alongside 27.5% FCF growth, give Klaviyo internal funding capacity. Strong recent cash production improves resilience and supports continued investment in products, infrastructure, and customer expansion.

New and adjacent products are gaining measurable usage: Composer reached more than 95,000 users in its first month, while analytics and data products grew ARR over 100%. This broadens the platform’s role, supports cross-sell, and can lift customer value over time.

bear.b: Gross margin fell about three percentage points year over year to 73.4% as text messaging became a larger mix and carrier fees increased. Although pricing changes are intended to pass through fees, these dynamics create ongoing execution pressure on margin sustainability.

Despite high gross margins and positive EBITDA, TTM net income was only about $6.8M, a roughly 0.5% net margin, while operating results remain near breakeven. Thin GAAP earnings leave less cushion if expenses rise or growth moderates, delaying stronger earnings conversion.

Net revenue retention of 109% indicates existing-customer expansion remains positive, but the expected pressure through Q1 next year can slow growth from the installed base. This makes near-term revenue durability more dependent on new wins and cross-selling while the effect rolls off.
